correctness.rationale: The established dephasing-to-pinch limit is reconstructed by finite-dimensional spectral convergence and averaging away endpoint times. All eigenprojectors of the combinatorial Laplacian of K_{m,n} are explicit, with coincident m=n eigenspaces merged; the entrywise-square matrix has four invariant sectors. Computing (F-F²)e_v gives a three-value vector. Its signs are proved globally using 4mn≤(m+n)² and 2(m-2)/m²>1/(2m) for integer m≥3; summing positive entries yields the exact rational two-branch formula. The n→∞ limit follows by a uniform rational bound for fixed m, and elementary differentiation gives the unique integer maximum m=5. A standard-library exact-rational certificate checked 70 graph pairs, and independent symmetric eigendecomposition checked 361 pairs. No finite test is used as proof of an infinite statement.

value.rationale: The complete-bipartite graph is a natural controlled test of whether the long-time, energy-dephased, two-time Kolmogorov defect necessarily decreases with network order, as happens for the source paper’s complete and cycle graph examples. The all-size classification reveals a sharp initial-part-size boundary: fixed m≤2 forces vanishing, while every fixed m≥3 sustains an order-one residual, and m=5 is the unique size that maximizes that asymptotic residual. The finding identifies a structural role of the local zero-sum Laplacian eigenspace and supplies an exact conditional-network-size benchmark not reducible to a tabulated integer. It does not claim general quantum sensing advantage, noise robustness, or optimal graph design beyond this well-defined family.
